summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified against live source. Implementation is clean, idiomatic, and well-tested.

SlugConflictError (ledger-store.ts:20–25): correct pattern — extends Error, sets this.name in constructor for reliable instanceof across transpilation boundaries. Named export, co-located with the single throw site and single consumer. No separate errors.ts warranted.

renameSlug() conflict path (ledger-store.ts:357): throws SlugConflictError correctly. The access()/ENOENT idiom is sound — resolves → conflict exists → throw; ENOENT → safe; other errors re-thrown unchanged.

handleRenameProject same-slug pre-check (api.ts:686–689): uses latestMeta ??= await store.readProjectMeta(). Nullish coalescing assignment is the right tool — correctly preserves any prior updateTitle() result rather than overwriting it.
handleRenameProject instanceof catch (api.ts:692): replaces fragile string-prefix matching with type-safe instanceof check; unexpected errors fall through to bare re-throw. Pattern is correct.

Both new tests (api.test.ts:658–688) are well-structured. Test 1 verifies last_updated is not mutated and directory still exists via access(). Test 2 verifies updateTitle() still fires in a combined request and slug is unchanged; last_updated check is consistent with existing AC.

comments.note: renameSlug() retains a plain Error throw for the same-slug guard (ledger-store.ts:350–353). This code path is correctly unreachable from handleRenameProject due to the pre-check, and documentation accurately labels it as such. Minor future maintenance consideration: if renameSlug() is ever called directly with the same slug, the caller receives a plain Error rather than SlugConflictError. Not a bug — just worth noting if the method's public surface ever widens.

The latestMeta! non-null assertion at api.ts end-of-function is documented in the JSDoc ('The non-null assertion keeps TypeScript happy'). This is the correct approach given the .refine() guarantee — cleaner than a redundant runtime check or a dummy default. No action needed.
No code issues found — implementation is clean, consistent with existing patterns, and correctly handles all error paths.
